title: How are planned routes saved and shared?
context: Hikers want to save a planned route, send it to friends, and load it on their GPS watch.

options.name: In the page link
options.summary: Encode the route in the web address.
assumptions: Routes stay under a few hundred points
risks: Some chat apps cut long links short

options.name: GPX file
options.summary: Save the route as a standard GPX file that watches and other apps read.
assumptions: Users are fine sending a file
risks: Notes the planner adds (rest stops, water) need GPX extensions that some apps ignore

estimates.basis: save, load and the notes extension

recommendation: Getting the route onto a watch is the main reason to save it, and only a GPX file does that.

evidence.claim: GPX is the common exchange format for routes and tracks across GPS devices and hiking apps.

reason: Friends load routes on their watches, so the file has to be GPX.

files.change: new: write the current route as a GPX 1.1 file, notes in an extension
new: read a GPX route or track, keep unknown parts, apply to the map
add save and load buttons with drawn icons

steps: Write save, with distances in kilometres and elevation in metres
Write load, keeping anything it does not understand
Round-trip test on three real routes and one watch
done_when: Saving then loading reproduces the route exactly
A saved route opens on a GPS watch and in one other hiking app
validation: Round-trip comparison of every point and note on three routes
avoid: Inventing a format of our own
Adding a settings toggle for this
